response: The determination between complete and incomplete traumatic spinal cord injury may not be as clinically relevant as previously thought. Research suggests that the combination of the acute phase voluntary anal contraction and the S4-5 LT and PP scores can predict significantly better chronic phase-independent ambulation outcomes than the currently used distinction between complete and incomplete spinal cord injury. This implies that the traditional classification may not be the most important factor in determining prognosis and treatment outcomes. Instead, other factors such as the presence of sacral sparing and the severity of the injury may be more relevant in predicting patient outcomes. Therefore, a more nuanced approach to assessing and treating traumatic spinal cord injuries may be necessary to improve patient care and outcomes.
